summary: Attacked the accepted extraction of Koenigsmann, 'Defining Z in Q' (Ann. of Math. 183 (2016) 73–93): 42 items, 2 source routes into LogicAndDefinabilityInNumberTheory, and 7 confirmed source issues. The item statements, the six library citations, the source hashes and the seven source issues all survived. So did a recheck of the case analyses of Propositions 6 and 10. There are nine findings, four medium and five low. Medium: (1) route 1 makes LD.4 consume Tau Ceti's QuadraticFormInvariants, GlobalQuadraticForms and weak approximation, but LD.4 has no prerequisite link to any of them; (2) model completeness and existential closedness, which Remark 24 uses, have no item and no owner; (3) the Colliot-Thélène–Van Geel theorem, the only input to Proposition 23(c), is a prerequisite but not an item; (4) the closure properties of diophantine sets are planned for Q only, while another extraction plans them for arbitrary rings in a proposed Part II after LD.4. Low: the archimedean Hilbert symbol is cited to a layer that is nonarchimedean only; Tau Ceti's quaternion norm form is uncited; the local square criterion has no item; two misprints are unrecorded (Z_l for Z_(l) on p. 90, and k + Z_(2) for k + 8Z_(2) on p. 91); and the §1 conditional transfer to Hilbert's tenth problem over Q has no item.
checked: Independence: this red team (Claude Code, session cc-f805bf) did neither the extraction (cc-39fac3, issue #1174, PR #3944) nor the review (cc-fb70e5, #4460). Read the complete extraction JSON (42 items, 2 routes, 7 sourceIssues, 2 sourceVersions), its report, the review JSON and research/blueprint/reviews/REV-PAPER-KOENIGSMANN-16.md, and PROTOCOL sections 0 and 15–18.

Source: re-fetched the published PDF (https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v183-n1-p02-p.pdf) and arXiv:1011.3424v2 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1011.3424v2) on 29 September 2026. SHA-256 f26c2e155d025978045a0c68073505631677624ef4d6f9b461640c6fbe1d3c93 and 6f10efddacba619eb816610b4a79edb28e6110f8b15d8d5813985eae1b58c541 both match the recorded values. Read all 21 published pages (§§1–4 and the references) in the text layer, and checked page images of p. 78 (the table), p. 90 (the proof of Proposition 21(e)) and p. 91 (the proof of Corollary 22). Collated arXiv v2 at the new misprints.

Item statements against the text, for all 42 items: Observation 0, Theorem 1 and Corollaries 2, 2′, 3 and 3′; Definition 4; Observation 5 with its Serre formulas; Facts (a)–(e); Proposition 6 and the convention for an empty intersection; Step 1's formula and the degree claim; Definitions 7, 9, 12 and 19; Remark 8; Proposition 10; Corollary 11; Lemmas 13, 14, 17 and 20; Corollary 15; Propositions 16, 18 and 21(a)–(e); Corollary 22; the §4 criterion; Proposition 23; Remark 24. Question 25 is correctly left out. Every numbered statement has an item, and no item statement is false. Item 26's corrected hypothesis and item 36's corrected identity are right.

The arguments, rechecked by hand: Remark 8(a) for mixed signs; Proposition 10(b) for negative p; Proposition 10(c) for all p, q; Lemma 13(b)–(d); Lemma 14's hypotheses in Corollary 15(b) and Proposition 16(b), including 2 ∉ P(p,q) from (−2p,q)₂ = 1; Proposition 16(a); Lemma 17(b); Proposition 18(a); Lemma 20(b) in both directions; the Legendre-symbol bookkeeping in the '⇒' step of Proposition 21(b); the soundness of the characterization at the end of Proposition 21(c); Proposition 21(e), all seven lines; Corollary 22 for every p ∈ Q^×; Proposition 23(d)'s algebraic-closure step; and the logic of Remark 24.

Numerically, with exact rational arithmetic in a scratch script: U_p for p = 2, 3, 5, 7, 11; all 16 rows of the p = 2 table (only (6, 15) fails, as E1 records; (15, 15) uses x₄ = 2/15, read off the page image); every row's pair has (a, b)₂ = −1; and Proposition 10(b)'s Δ-intersections for every integer 0 < |p| ≤ 300 and k = 3, 5, 7, with no failures.

All seven recorded sourceIssues at their locators. E1 was verified on the p. 78 image and by computation. E2, E3, E6 and E7 were verified in the text, and E4 in the text and on the p. 91 image. E5 was verified by the a = b = 1 computation. The correction in E6, {±1, ±2}·(Q^×)²·Φ′₅Φ′₅·Φ′₇Φ′₇, was verified by the case split on the number of P^{[5]} and P^{[7]} primes. All seven stand. Two further misprints were found (finding 8).

Every library citation read at the pin, via declarations.tsv and then the file. Mathlib 082e2d3: FirstOrder.Language.ring (ModelTheory/Algebra/Ring/Basic.lean:60); Set.Definable (ModelTheory/Definability.lean:56); BoundedFormula.IsExistential and IsUniversal (ModelTheory/Complexity.lean:343, 331) with realize_embedding (399, 388); legendreSym.quadratic_reciprocity (QuadraticReciprocity.lean:107); ZMod.exists_sq_eq_two_iff (:74); ZMod.exists_sq_eq_neg_one_iff (LegendreSymbol/Basic.lean:285); Nat.forall_exists_prime_gt_and_eq_mod (LSeries/PrimesInAP.lean:442, Dirichlet for a unit class, not deprecated); Nat.sum_four_squares (SumFourSquares.lean:199); Localization.AtPrime; Ideal.jacobson; QuaternionAlgebra (Algebra/Quaternion.lean:65); padicValRat; Dioph.pow_dioph (Dioph.lean:667); Pell.matiyasevic; ElementaryEmbedding; ElementarySubstructure. Tau Ceti f790474: TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.weakApproximation_denseRange (NumberTheory/NumberField/Global/Approximation/Weak.lean:202, Artin–Whaples at finitely many finite and infinite places). Every citation gives its item. The one gap is item 8's archimedean clause (finding 5).

Searched both libraries for everything marked missing: hilbertSymbol, Hilbert symbol, Hasse–Minkowski, hasse norm, isGlobalNorm, product formula, quaternion splitting and ramification, model completeness, existential closedness, Diophantine sets over rings or fields, REPred and MRDP. Nothing supplies a missing item. Mathlib's Dioph API (Dioph.inter, Dioph.union, ex_dioph, …) is over ℕ only. The search found Tau Ceti's quaternion norm form (finding 6), Mathlib's hensels_lemma (finding 7) and Rat.isSquare_iff_even_factorization (PadicVal/Basic.lean:398), which is useful for Proposition 21(b).

Every planned stage, with its full text read in research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps: LD.0 and LD.4 (with the campaign README), QuadraticFormInvariants layer 2 and 6C (all 15 milestones), GlobalQuadraticForms layers 0, 4, 5 and 6, and ClassicalArithmeticCompletion CA.1 and CA.4. Also read the LD packet (13 LD.4 nodes, all on Mathlib's Dioph normal form) and the reviewed audit entries for QFI layer 2 ('partly built') and 6C ('not built'). Items 7, 9 and 10 are planned where cited. Item 8's ∞ clause is not (finding 5). Items 2 and 39 fit LD.4 and LD.0. Every stage id resolves.

Routing and ownership: all 31 missing items are routed exactly once (30 to LD.4, 1 to LD.0), and nothing that is not missing is routed. The review's move of items 40 and 41 to LD.4 avoids an LD.0 → LD.4 → LD.0 cycle and is correct. Checked LD.4's prerequisites and edges and the GlobalQuadraticForms link map (finding 1). Searched every paper extraction and new roadmap for overlapping owners: PAPER-ALPOGE-BHARGAVA-SHNIDMAN-26, whose Hilbert's-tenth Part II is rejected pending revision (finding 4); PAPER-DITTMANN-POP-23, which routes interpretations to LD.0 and a finitely-generated-fields Part II but plans nothing specific to Q; and PAPER-CARO-PASTEN-23, which has no overlap. No other roadmap, packet or reserved id plans quaternion trace sets or the definability of Z in Q, so the route owner is right and no new roadmap is needed.

Review changes: item 11 moved to library, item 42 added, items 40 and 41 moved to route 1, item 26 corrected, and new mistakes E5–E7. Each was checked and none introduced an error. The review's statement that 6C 'plans exactly these statements' is too strong for item 8's ∞ clause (finding 5). Its statement that nothing quaternion-related exists at the pins misses the norm form (finding 6).
Not done: Poonen's Amer. J. Math. paper was not reread, so the '9244' degree claim rests on the review's check. [CTVG14], [PD11] and Park were not opened. No Lean was run or written.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-KOENIGSMANN-16.result.json, routes[0] (source → LogicAndDefinabilityInNumberTheory:LD.4), its reason; and the LD.4 stage record
findings.claim: Route 1 sends 30 items to LD.4 and justifies it by saying their inputs are 'already planned or built' in Tau Ceti's QuadraticFormInvariants (layer 2, 6C), GlobalQuadraticForms (layers 4 and 6) and Tau Ceti's weak approximation. But LD.4 imports none of these layers, its roadmap does not list either quadratic-form roadmap or Global Number Fields as a prerequisite, and the only link map that screened the pair records no edge. So once the route is applied, the LD.4 blueprint would consume Hilbert symbols, Hilbert reciprocity, the quaternion splitting criterion, Hasse–Minkowski representation, the quadratic Hasse norm theorem and weak approximation across a roadmap boundary that has no prerequisite link. Section 15 requires such imports to go through a prerequisite link to the owning layer. The extraction's report says 'The route also records the stage's dependencies on … the Tau Ceti quadratic-form roadmaps', but that record is prose in the route reason only, and nothing in the JSON or the atlas carries it.

The roadmap record's "prerequisites" are ["ClassicalArithmeticCompletion","DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence","MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles","SchemeAndStackFoundations"]. Its stageEdges into LD.4 are exactly CA.4 → LD.4 and LD.0 → LD.4. research/blueprint/links/tauceti_TauCetiRoadmap_GlobalQuadraticForms.json line 158: {"roadmapId":"LogicAndDefinabilityInNumberTheory","result":"none","note":"Summary only; no edge asserted. Stage-level screen pending."}. There is no link map for QuadraticFormInvariants in research/blueprint/links/. Items 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11 of the extraction cite exactly these layers as the suppliers of the inputs that route 1's items use (Proposition 6 uses Observation 5, Fact (e) and approximation; Proposition 16(a) uses Hilbert reciprocity; Proposition 21(e) uses the local–global principle for norms).
findings.fix: In routes[0] of PAPER-KOENIGSMANN-16.result.json, add to the reason an explicit list of the cross-roadmap stages the LD.4 blueprint must import for these items: tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/QuadraticFormInvariants#layer-2-quaternion-algebras-and-the-four-fold-splitting-criterion and #6c-the-hilbert-symbol-and-the-local-hasse-invariant (items 7–9); tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/GlobalQuadraticForms#layer-4-global-square-norm-and-approximation-lemmas and #layer-6-representation-and-isometry (items 8–10); and Tau Ceti's TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.weakApproximation_denseRange (item 11). Correct the report's sentence that the route 'records' these dependencies so that it says where they are recorded.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-KOENIGSMANN-16.result.json: no item for model completeness or existential closedness; item PAPER-KOENIGSMANN-16/41 (Remark 24) and routes[1] (LD.0)
findings.claim: The paper defines model completeness and existential closedness, and it uses the fact that a model-complete theory makes every definable set existentially definable. That fact is the only step from 'not every definable subset of Q is diophantine' to 'Th(Q) is not model complete' in Remark 24. The extraction has no item for these definitions or this implication. Item 41 states Remark 24 using them, and item 39 (the preservation criterion) covers only existential definability of one definable set. LD.0, where the extraction routes item 39, does not plan model completeness: its specification lists languages, structures, formulas, definable sets, interpretations, ultraproducts, Łoś and an elementary extension. Mathlib at the pin has neither notion.
findings.evidence: Published p. 92: 'The strongest closure property a complete first-order theory (whose models are infinite) might have is that it is model complete, that is, that if one model of the theory is a substructure of another model, it is an elementary substructure or, equivalently, that the smaller model is existentially closed in the larger model.' The proof of Remark 24 ends: 'So not every definable subset of Q is diophantine in Q, and hence Q is not model complete. Or, in other words, there are models Q⋆, Q⋆⋆ of Th(Q) with Q⋆ ⊆ Q⋆⋆ where Q⋆ is not existentially closed in Q⋆⋆.' LD.0 (content/campaign/LogicAndDefinabilityInNumberTheory/README.md:17): 'Define first-order ring/valued-field languages, structures, formulas, definable sets and interpretation in arithmetic fields; … Construct ultraproducts and prove the needed Los transfer theorem; nonstandard arithmetic uses an explicit elementary extension …'. At Mathlib 082e2d3, a search of Mathlib/ModelTheory for 'model complete', 'existentially closed' and 'IsExistentiallyClosed' finds nothing; the only hits for 'model_complete' are model_completeTheory and realize_iff_of_model_completeTheory (Mathlib/ModelTheory/Semantics.lean:784, 789), which concern a structure's complete theory. declarations.tsv has no declaration whose name contains ModelComplete or ExistentiallyClosed, in either library.
findings.fix: Add an item (kind definition + theorem), locator 'Section 4, p. 92, paragraph before Remark 24 and proof of Remark 24': 'A substructure M ⊆ N of L-structures is existentially closed if every existential formula with parameters from M that holds in N holds in M. A theory T is model complete if every embedding between models of T is elementary. Equivalently, every model of T is existentially closed in every model of T that extends it. If T is model complete, then every formula is T-equivalent to an existential formula; in particular every definable subset of a model is existentially definable.' Status missing. Cite Mathlib's FirstOrder.Language.ElementaryEmbedding and FirstOrder.Language.BoundedFormula.IsExistential as the base. Add it to routes[1] (LD.0), next to item 39, from which the last clause follows. Record in item 41's note that it depends on this item.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-KOENIGSMANN-16.result.json: item PAPER-KOENIGSMANN-16/40 (Proposition 23(c)); the theorem it uses appears only under prerequisites
findings.claim: Proposition 23(c) is proved entirely by the theorem of Colliot-Thélène and Van Geel: for every n, the set of non-n-th powers is diophantine in a number field. That is a deep external theorem, and Koenigsmann's elementary methods give only n = 2 (Proposition 21(b)). The extraction does not make it an item. It appears only in `prerequisites` and in a clause of item 40's note ('(c) needs Colliot-Thélène–Van Geel'). Item 40 is routed as 'missing' to LD.4, so the LD.4 blueprint receives Proposition 23(c) with no item or owner for its one substantive input. The extraction does itemize Poonen's lemmas (item 17), [PD11, Lemma 3.1.6] (item 39) and Dirichlet's theorem (item 4), each an external result used in a proof. Section 16 asks for 'every definition, construction and key theorem the paper uses or proves on the way to its main results', and each stated result is itself an item here.
findings.evidence: Published p. 91–92, proof of Proposition 23(c): '(c) The nontrivial inclusion follows since the property of not being an n-th power is, by the main result in [CTVG14], diophantine in Q. (For n = 2, this was shown in [Poo09b], an elementary proof being given in our Proposition 21(b).)' Also p. 90: 'It has recently been generalized in [CTVG14] to all n-th powers: for any natural number n, the set of non-n-th powers is diophantine in Q.' In the extraction, `prerequisites` has the entry 'J.-L. Colliot-Thélène and J. Van Geel, … Compositio Math. 151 (2015)', and item 40's statement ends '(c) (Q**)ⁿ ∩ Q* = (Q*)ⁿ for all n (via [CTVG14])'. No item has the CTVG statement. Searching declarations.tsv at both pins for non-n-th powers, for a Diophantine predicate over a field, or for 'Colliot' finds nothing: Mathlib's `Dioph` is over ℕ only (Mathlib/NumberTheory/Dioph.lean).
findings.fix: Add an item (kind theorem), 'Colliot-Thélène–Van Geel: for every number field K and every integer n ≥ 1, the set {x ∈ K : x is not an n-th power in K} is diophantine in K', with locator 'Section 3, p. 90; proof of Proposition 23(c), pp. 91–92 ([CTVG14])' and status missing. Route it with item 40 to LD.4 as an external theorem input that needs its own source decomposition, so that the LD.4 blueprint takes [CTVG14] as a source for it. Change item 40's note to cite the new item.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-KOENIGSMANN-16.result.json: items PAPER-KOENIGSMANN-16/42 and /1 (diophantine sets), /15 (Corollary 3), routed to LD.4; compare research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-ALPOGE-BHARGAVA-SHNIDMAN-26.result.json items /1, /3, /46, /47
findings.claim: Item 42 plans the closure properties of diophantine sets (conjunction, disjunction, projection, preimage, recursive enumerability) only for subsets of Qⁿ, and puts them in LD.4. Another extraction in the atlas plans the same notion for an arbitrary commutative ring. That is PAPER-ALPOGE-BHARGAVA-SHNIDMAN-26, which has 'Diophantine subsets of a ring' (/1), 'Finite intersections of Diophantine sets' (/47), 'Transitivity of Diophantine definitions' (/46) and 'Transfer of undecidability along Diophantine definitions' (/3). It routes them to a proposed 'Logic, definability, valued fields and motivic integration, Part II: Hilbert's tenth problem over rings of integers', which 'start[s] after LD.4'. Koenigsmann's Corollary 3 (item 15) is an instance of that transfer step. Section 15 requires a general notion to be planned once, in the most general form its uses need, in the most foundational owner. As routed, LD.4 would plan a ℚ-only version, and the Part II would plan the general one again. The Part II route is now rejected pending revision (review route 5), so this is a duplication that is about to happen, not one already in two accepted plans.
findings.evidence: Item 42's statement: 'Diophantine subsets of Qⁿ are closed under finite intersections (f = 0 ∧ g = 0 ⟺ f² + g² = 0), finite unions (fg = 0), projections and polynomial preimages, and the sets {x ≠ 0} … and {x ≥ 0} … are diophantine; … Every diophantine subset of Qⁿ is recursively enumerable.' PAPER-ALPOGE-BHARGAVA-SHNIDMAN-26.result.json, item /1: 'For a commutative ring R with identity and k ≥ 0, a subset E ⊆ R^k is Diophantine if finitely many polynomials f_i … satisfy t ∈ E iff there exists x ∈ R^n with every f_i(t,x)=0'; item /47: 'A finite intersection of Diophantine subsets of R^k is Diophantine'; its part-ii route's brief: 'Start after LD.4’s negative solution of Hilbert’s tenth problem over Z. … Build Diophantine subsets of arbitrary commutative rings and finite tuples with the APIs/tests in items 1 and 45–50'. research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-ALPOGE-BHARGAVA-SHNIDMAN-26.review.json, route 5: verdict 'reject' ('The proposed LD.4 successor has the right direction, but …'). Koenigsmann p. 74: 'Together with the undecidability of Th∃(Z), Theorem 1 immediately implies Corollary 3.'
findings.fix: Restate item 42 for an arbitrary commutative ring R: diophantine subsets of Rⁿ, defined by finite polynomial systems, are closed under finite intersection, finite union, projection and polynomial preimage, and diophantine definitions compose, since a set that is diophantine over a diophantine subring is diophantine. Keep the ℚ-specific clauses as separate clauses of the item: over a field one equation suffices, since f² + g² = 0 needs a formally real field; {x ≠ 0} is diophantine; {x ≥ 0} is diophantine over ℚ; and diophantine sets over a computable ring are r.e. Add a note that PAPER-ALPOGE-BHARGAVA-SHNIDMAN-26 items /1, /3, /46 and /47 consume this item, so that LD.4 is their single owner and the revised Part II imports them rather than re-planning them. Also leave a maintainer note that the revision of PAPER-ALPOGE-BHARGAVA-SHNIDMAN-26 route 5 should cite LD.4 for them.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-KOENIGSMANN-16.result.json: item PAPER-KOENIGSMANN-16/8 (Observation 5), its planned list and note
findings.claim: Item 8 includes the archimedean clause '(a,b)_∞ = −1 iff a < 0 and b < 0' and cites QuadraticFormInvariants 6C and ClassicalArithmeticCompletion CA.1. The review says 6C 'plans exactly these statements'. But 6C covers only nonarchimedean local fields. The archimedean Hilbert symbol is planned in GlobalQuadraticForms layer 4 (4.4), which says 6C cannot supply it. CA.1 only says to 'record residue symbols at 2 and at infinite places'. So the ∞ clause of Observation 5, used in Proposition 6 (Fact (c)), Lemma 13 and Proposition 21(e), is cited to a layer that does not plan it.
findings.evidence: GlobalQuadraticForms, layer 4.4 (content/tau-ceti/GlobalQuadraticForms/README.md:463–467, also in research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/tauceti_TauCetiRoadmap_GlobalQuadraticForms.json): '**The archimedean symbol.** At a real place `(a,b) = -1` exactly when both `a < 0` and `b < 0`, and at a complex place it is always `1`. Both are computations with the norm equation `b = x² − a y²` and are proved here, because Quadratic Form Invariants' Layer 6C carries `IsNonarchimedeanLocalField` on every theorem about the symbol.' QFI 6C's milestones 9–12 are the closed formulas for odd residue characteristic, for ℚ_2 and for a finite dyadic extension, and the 8×8 table over ℚ_2; none is archimedean. CA.1 (research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/ClassicalArithmeticCompletion.json): 'Record residue symbols at 2 and at infinite places.'
findings.fix: Add tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/GlobalQuadraticForms#layer-4-global-square-norm-and-approximation-lemmas to item 8's `planned` list. In its note, say that the p = ∞ clause is GlobalQuadraticForms 4.4 ('the archimedean symbol') and that 6C supplies the finite places only.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-KOENIGSMANN-16.result.json: items PAPER-KOENIGSMANN-16/6 (quaternion algebras) and /16 (S_{a,b} as traces of norm-one elements); the review's statement that nothing quaternion-related exists at the pins
findings.claim: The equation that defines S_{a,b} is the norm-one condition for Koenigsmann's H_{a,b}: x₁² − ax₂² − bx₃² + abx₄² = 1 is Nrd(x) = 1 for the diagonal norm form ⟨1, −a, −b, ab⟩. The traces are 2x₁. At the pin, Tau Ceti has that norm form on Mathlib's QuaternionAlgebra and its diagonalization ⟨1, −a, −b, ab⟩, and the reviewed library audit records it. Item 6 cites only Mathlib's QuaternionAlgebra, and item 16's note is silent. The review says 'nothing on quaternion trace sets, definability of Z in Q, Hilbert symbols or Hasse–Minkowski exists at the pins'. That is true of the trace sets themselves, but it misses the norm-form base on which a blueprint of item 16 builds. The item's status, missing, is right.
findings.evidence: Tau Ceti f790474, TauCeti/Algebra/Quaternion/NormForm.lean:72: 'def normForm : QuadraticForm R ℍ[R,c₁,c₂,c₃]', documented as 'the reduced norm x ↦ (x * star x).re'. Line 171: '/-- **The norm form of `ℍ[R,a,b]` is `⟨1, -a, -b, ab⟩`.** -/ theorem equivalent_normForm_weightedSumSquares : (normForm a 0 b).Equivalent (weightedSumSquares R ![(1 : R), -a, -b, a * b])'. Line 204: equivalent_pureNormForm_weightedSumSquares for ⟨−a, −b, ab⟩. Line 113: normForm_mul, multiplicativity. All four are in declarations.tsv under the names QuaternionAlgebra.normForm, QuaternionAlgebra.equivalent_normForm_weightedSumSquares, QuaternionAlgebra.equivalent_pureNormForm_weightedSumSquares and QuaternionAlgebra.normForm_mul. data/library-coverage.json, layer tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/QuadraticFormInvariants#layer-2-…: verdict 'partly built' (AUDIT-05), target 'The norm form Nrd as a QuadraticForm on ℍ[K,a,b], with Nrd ≅ ⟨1,−a,−b,ab⟩, the pure part ⟨−a,−b,ab⟩, and multiplicativity', library 'tauceti'.
findings.fix: Add tauceti:QuaternionAlgebra.normForm and tauceti:QuaternionAlgebra.equivalent_normForm_weightedSumSquares to item 6's `library` list. Add a note to item 16: S_{a,b} = {2·re(x) : x ∈ ℍ[ℚ,a,b], normForm a 0 b x = 1}, built on those declarations with Mathlib's QuaternionAlgebra.re, so the new material is only the sets S, T and their local versions. In item 7's note, say that QFI layer 2 is 'partly built' per the audit, with its splitting criterion still absent.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-KOENIGSMANN-16.result.json: no item for the local square criterion (Hensel's lemma at 2 and at odd primes)
findings.claim: Several proofs use the local square criterion, but no item carries it. The p = 2 table in Proposition 6 needs 1 + 8Z₂ ⊆ (Q₂^×)². Proposition 21(b) '⇐' passes from x ∈ 2·(Q^×)²·(1 + lZ_l) to x ∈ 2·(Q_l^×)². Lemma 20 and Proposition 21(b) '⇒' identify a residue that is a nonsquare mod q with a class in 2·(Q^×)²·(1 + qZ_(q)). Observation 5 is read throughout as a condition on residues. The item list has quadratic reciprocity, Dirichlet and weak approximation, but not this fact. Mathlib has Hensel's lemma over Z_p, and Tau Ceti's QuadraticFormInvariants 6A plans the sharp local square theorem.
findings.evidence: Published p. 78: 'Multiplying x₂², x₃², x₄² by a suitable common element from 1 + 8Z₂ ⊆ (Q₂^×)² then makes sure that 2x₁ ∈ S_{a,b}(Q₂).' Published p. 88, proof of Proposition 21(b): 'P^{[3]}(p) contains a prime l, and J(R_p^{[3]}) ⊆ lZ_l. Thus x ∈ 2(Q_l^×)².' Mathlib 082e2d3, Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/Hensel.lean:461: 'theorem hensels_lemma : ∃ z : ℤ_[p], F.aeval z = 0 ∧ ‖z - a‖ < ‖F.derivative.aeval a‖ ∧ …' under 'hnorm : ‖F.aeval a‖ < ‖F.derivative.aeval a‖ ^ 2'. findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-KOENIGSMANN-16.result.json: sourceIssues (E1–E7), which omit two misprints in the proofs of Proposition 21(e) and Corollary 22
findings.claim: The extraction and its review record seven mistakes, but they miss two misprints in the published text. Both are also in arXiv v2. (1) In the proof of Proposition 21(e), '⇒' direction, the text says 'Let p = l. Then R_p^{[k]} = Z_l'. But R_p^{[k]} is a subring of Q, and by Proposition 10(b) it equals Z_(l) for a prime l ≡ k mod 8; Z_l, the l-adic integers, is not a subset of Q. (2) In the proof of Corollary 22, 'p ∉ Φ_k' is rewritten as 'p ∉ Z_(2)^× or (p ∈ k + Z_(2) and p ∉ Φ_k)' and called 'diophantine by Proposition 21(c)'. But Proposition 21(c) is about 'x ≡ k (mod 8Z_(2)) and x ∉ Φ_k', and the same sentence's assumption is written 'p ∈ Q²·(k + 8Z_(2))', so 'k + Z_(2)' should be 'k + 8Z_(2)'. As printed, the clause is still logically equivalent under the assumption, since a 2-adic unit in Q²·(k + 8Z_(2)) is already ≡ k mod 8Z_(2). So both misprints affect nothing.
findings.evidence: Published p. 90 (page image checked at 150 dpi): '‘⇒’: Assume l ∈ P^{[k]} with (x, y)_l = −1. Let p = l. Then R_p^{[k]} = Z_l and ‘(···)’ says that v_l(x) is odd …'. Published p. 91 (page image checked): 'Note that, under the assumption ‘p ∈ Q²·(k + 8Z_(2)),’ the property ‘p ∉ Φ_k’ is equivalent to ‘p ∉ Z^×_(2) or (p ∈ k + Z_(2) and p ∉ Φ_k),’ which is diophantine by Proposition 21(c).' Proposition 21(c), p. 87: 'for fixed k ∈ {1, 3, 5, 7}, the property that x ≡ k (mod 8Z_(2)) and x ∉ Φ_k'. arXiv:1011.3424v2 has the same two sentences: p. 20 ('Let p = l. Then R_p = Z_l') and p. 21 ('(p ∈ k + Z(2) and p ∉ Φk)', with 'k + 8Z(2)' in the same sentence's assumption). This is from the text layer, and the '8' of the assumption is extracted there, so it was not dropped by pdftotext.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-KOENIGSMANN-16.result.json: no item for the conditional transfer in §1 (Z diophantine in Q ⇒ Hilbert's tenth problem over Q has a negative answer); compare items /12, /15 and /40
findings.claim: The paper frames its main theorem with a precise implication: if Z had an existential definition in Q, Th∃(Z) would be interpretable in Th∃(Q), and by Matiyasevich's theorem the existential theory of Q, Hilbert's tenth problem over Q, would be undecidable. This is the conditional statement behind Observation 0 and behind Question 25's remark ('a negative answer would imply that Z is not diophantine in Q'). It is the 'interpretation theorem' that LD.4's acceptance criterion asks for in the rational case. Corollary 3 (item 15) is the unconditional ∀∃ version, but the existential version has no item.
findings.evidence: Published p. 73: 'If one had an existential (or diophantine) definition of Z in Q (i.e., a definition by an existential first-order L_ring-formula), then Th∃(Z) would be interpretable in Th∃(Q), and the answer would, by Matiyasevich’s Theorem, again be no. But it is still open whether Z is existentially definable in Q.' LD.4 acceptance (content/campaign/LogicAndDefinabilityInNumberTheory/README.md, LD.4): 'Integer undecidability is not copied to rational or arbitrary number fields; each transfer needs its own interpretation theorem.' Items 12 (Observation 0), 15 (Corollary 3) and 40 (Proposition 23(d), which assumes Z diophantine) do not state this implication.
findings.fix: Add an item (kind theorem), locator '§1, p. 73': 'If Z is diophantine in Q, then Th∃(Q) is undecidable, so Hilbert's tenth problem over Q has a negative answer. The proof relativizes each existential sentence over Z to the diophantine definition of Z and applies item 2.' Status missing. Route it with items 12 and 15 in routes[0] (LD.4). It is the ∃-level instance of the transfer in item 15, and the general transfer of PAPER-ALPOGE-BHARGAVA-SHNIDMAN-26/3 specializes to it (see finding 4).
